title: Blog 1
content:
Uploading to Amazon S3 directly from a web or mobile application Item Detail Original post Uploading to Amazon S3 directly from a web or mobile application Source AWS Compute Blog · James Beswick · 2020 Topic Serverless · Storage Translated on [dd/mm/2026] Summary The post shows how to let a browser or mobile app upload files straight to Amazon S3 instead of through an application server. The client calls an API Gateway endpoint, Lambda creates a presigned URL valid for 300 seconds with a random object key, and the client sends the file directly to S3. This reduces server load and network traffic; the post also notes that the bucket needs CORS rules and that a JWT authorizer should restrict who can upload.
Relevance to SnapThumb SnapThumb uses exactly this pattern in steps 2–5. One difference: SnapThumb uses a presigned POST instead of a presigned PUT, because POST supports a content-length-range condition so S3 itself rejects files over 10 MB, a limit the original post leaves unaddressed.
Translation [The Vietnamese translation lives on the Vietnamese version of this page]

title: Create the API Lambda
content:
Step 1: Create the function Lambda → Create function, name snapthumb-api, Python 3.12 → Create function. Replace lambda_function.py with the code below → Deploy. """SnapThumb - hàm Lambda cho API (API Gateway HTTP API, payload 2.0). POST /uploads -> kiểm tra file, tạo bản ghi PENDING, trả về presigned POST để trình duyệt upload thẳng lên S3 GET /images -> danh sách ảnh mới nhất kèm link xem có thời hạn DELETE /images/{id} -> xoá ảnh gốc, thumbnail và bản ghi """ import json import logging import os import uuid from datetime import datetime, timezone from decimal import Decimal import boto3 from botocore.config import Config logger = logging.getLogger() logger.setLevel(logging.INFO) ALLOWED_TYPES = {"image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp"} MAX_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024 UPLOAD_EXPIRES = 300 # giây: link upload hết hạn sau 5 phút VIEW_EXPIRES = 3600 # giây: link xem ảnh hết hạn sau 1 giờ LIST_LIMIT = 50 _s3 = None _table = None def s3(): global _s3 if _s3 is None: region = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1") # Endpoint theo region để link upload đi thẳng tới đúng region của bucket. _s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name=region, endpoint_url=f"https://s3.{region}.amazonaws.com", config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "virtual"})) return _s3 def table(): global _table if _table is None: _table = boto3.resource("dynamodb").Table(os.environ["TABLE_NAME"]) return _table def bucket(): return os.environ["BUCKET_NAME"] def _json_default(value): if isinstance(value, Decimal): return int(value) if value == value.to_integral_value() else float(value) raise TypeError(type(value)) def reply(status, payload=None): res = {"statusCode": status, "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"}} if payload is not None: res["body"] = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, default=_json_default) return res def create_upload(event): try: body = json.loads(event.get("body") or "{}") except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError): return reply(400, {"error": "Body must be JSON"}) filename = str(body.get("filename") or "").strip()[:200] content_type = str(body.get("contentType") or "") size = body.get("size") if not filename: return reply(400, {"error": "filename is required"}) if content_type not in ALLOWED_TYPES: return reply(400, {"error": "Only JPEG, PNG and WebP images are allowed"}) if not isinstance(size, int) or size <= 0 or size > MAX_BYTES: return reply(400, {"error": f"File size must be between 1 byte and {MAX_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)} MB"}) image_id = uuid.uuid4().hex key = f"uploads/{image_id}.{ALLOWED_TYPES[content_type]}" table().put_item(Item={ "id": image_id, "filename": filename, "contentType": content_type, "originalKey": key, "status": "PENDING", "createdAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), }) upload = s3().generate_presigned_post( Bucket=bucket(), Key=key, Fields={"Content-Type": content_type}, # S3 tự từ chối nếu file sai loại hoặc lớn hơn giới hạn, kể cả khi trình duyệt khai báo sai. Conditions=[{"Content-Type": content_type}, ["content-length-range", 1, MAX_BYTES]], ExpiresIn=UPLOAD_EXPIRES, ) return reply(201, {"id": image_id, "upload": upload}) def view_url(key): return s3().generate_presigned_url("get_object", Params={"Bucket": bucket(), "Key": key}, ExpiresIn=VIEW_EXPIRES) def list_images(event): items, kwargs = [], {} while True: page = table().scan(**kwargs) items.extend(page.get("Items", [])) if "LastEvaluatedKey" not in page or len(items) >= 500: break kwargs["ExclusiveStartKey"] = page["LastEvaluatedKey"] items.sort(key=lambda i: i.get("createdAt", ""), reverse=True) items = items[:LIST_LIMIT] for item in items: item["originalUrl"] = view_url(item["originalKey"]) if item.get("thumbKey"): item["thumbUrl"] = view_url(item["thumbKey"]) return reply(200, {"images": items}) def delete_image(event): image_id = (event.get("pathParameters") or {}).get("id", "") item = table().get_item(Key={"id": image_id}).get("Item") if not item: return reply(404, {"error": "Image not found"}) keys = [item["originalKey"]] + ([item["thumbKey"]] if item.get("thumbKey") else []) s3().delete_objects(Bucket=bucket(), Delete={"Objects": [{"Key": k} for k in keys]}) table().delete_item(Key={"id": image_id}) return reply(204) ROUTES = { "POST /uploads": create_upload, "GET /images": list_images, "DELETE /images/{id}": delete_image, } def handler(event, context): route = ROUTES.get(event.get("routeKey", "")) if not route: return reply(404, {"error": "Not found"}) try: return route(event) except Exception: logger.exception("Unhandled error on %s", event.get("routeKey")) return reply(500, {"error": "Internal error"}) lambda_handler = handler # tên hàm mặc định của Lambda console / default handler name in the console What the code does Part Explanation ROUTES Maps API Gateway’s routeKey (e.g. POST /uploads) to a Python function create_upload Checks name, type (JPEG/PNG/WebP) and size (≤ 10 MB), writes PENDING, calls generate_presigned_post Conditions Rules baked into the signature: S3 rejects a file of another type or over 10 MB list_images Reads all items, sorts newest first, adds generate_presigned_url view links _json_default DynamoDB returns numbers as Decimal; this converts them for JSON Step 2: Configuration Timeout 10 sec. Environment variables: TABLE_NAME = snapthumb-images, BUCKET_NAME = snapthumb-images-<your-name>. Step 3: Permissions Add an inline policy snapthumb-api-access to the function’s role:
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "Metadata", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:PutItem", "dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:Scan", "dynamodb:DeleteItem"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:ACCOUNT_ID:table/snapthumb-images" }, { "Sid": "SignUploads", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::snapthumb-images-YOURNAME/uploads/*" }, { "Sid": "SignViewsAndDelete", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:DeleteObject"], "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::snapthumb-images-YOURNAME/*" } ] } Signing a link makes no call to S3, but the link only works if the signer is allowed to do what the link does. That is why the API role needs s3:PutObject on uploads/* even though it never uploads anything itself.

title: Publish the Pillow Layer
content:
Why a layer Pillow contains compiled code, so it must be built for Lambda’s Linux and Python 3.12, not for your laptop. The command below asks pip for the right Linux wheel.
Build and publish in CloudShell Open CloudShell (the >_ icon at the top of the console), in ap-southeast-1. Run: mkdir -p pillow-layer/python python3 -m pip install --target pillow-layer/python \ --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 \ --implementation cp --python-version 3.12 --only-binary=:all: Pillow==11.0.0 cd pillow-layer && zip -qr ../pillow-layer.zip python && cd .. aws lambda publish-layer-version --layer-name pillow-py312 \ --zip-file fileb://pillow-layer.zip \ --compatible-runtimes python3.12 --compatible-architectures x86_64 \ --query LayerVersionArn --output text The last command prints the layer ARN, e.g. arn:aws:lambda:ap-southeast-1:123456789012:layer:pillow-py312:1. 📷 Insert screenshot: CloudShell output with the layer ARN → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/01-layer.png
A Python layer must put libraries under a python/ folder inside the zip; Lambda adds that folder to the import path.

title: Worklog
content:
Worklog This section records my 12-week internship. The first five weeks covered core AWS services (IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway). From week 6 I worked on my project, SnapThumb, an event-driven image thumbnail service built with Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon API Gateway.
Week 1: Program onboarding and securing the AWS account
Week 2: Networking and compute: Amazon VPC, Amazon EC2
Week 3: Storage: Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront
Week 4: Databases: Amazon RDS and Amazon DynamoDB
Week 5: Serverless: AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway
Week 6: Event-driven architecture; choosing the project
Week 7: Image storage and Pillow on Lambda
Week 8: Thumbnail Lambda triggered by S3
Week 9: API and web frontend
Week 10: Automating with CloudFormation and testing
Week 11: Writing the workshop and publishing the report on GitHub Pages
Week 12: Internship wrap-up

title: Workshop Overview
content:
How SnapThumb works The system has two Lambda functions with different jobs:
Component AWS service What it does Web page Amazon S3 (static website) Drag-and-drop upload and a gallery of thumbnails Front door Amazon API Gateway HTTPS endpoints the page calls API Lambda AWS Lambda Validates files, signs time-limited upload and view links, lists and deletes images Image storage Amazon S3 (private bucket) Originals under uploads/, thumbnails under thumbnails/ Thumbnail Lambda AWS Lambda + Pillow Runs automatically for each new image and creates its thumbnail Image records Amazon DynamoDB Status (PENDING → DONE / FAILED), dimensions, sizes, processing time Logs Amazon CloudWatch Every run of both functions Key concepts Event-driven architecture Nothing polls the bucket. When an object is created, S3 emits an event and invokes the Lambda function directly. The function runs only when there is work, and AWS runs many copies in parallel when many images arrive.
S3 Event Notifications A bucket setting that says “when an object is created under this prefix, call this target”. SnapThumb listens only to uploads/. Thumbnails are written to thumbnails/, so writing a thumbnail never triggers the function again. Without this split, the function would trigger itself in an endless loop.
Presigned URL / presigned POST A link signed with the API Lambda’s permissions that lets the browser upload one specific object directly to S3 for a short time (5 minutes). The browser never gets AWS credentials, and large files never pass through Lambda. The presigned POST also carries conditions: S3 rejects files that are not the declared type or are larger than 10 MB.
Lambda layer A zip of libraries shared by functions. Pillow (the Python imaging library) is not included in the Lambda runtime, so you publish it once as a layer and attach it to the Thumbnail function.
DynamoDB on-demand A NoSQL table billed per request, with no capacity to plan. Each image is one item keyed by id.
Test each part before moving on: upload a file to the bucket by hand and check that a thumbnail appears (5.5) → call the API with curl (5.6) → use the web page (5.7).

title: Blog 2
content:
Resize Images on the Fly with Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, and Amazon API Gateway Item Detail Original post Resize Images on the Fly with Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, and Amazon API Gateway Source AWS Compute Blog · John Pignata · 2017 Topic Serverless · Image processing Translated on [dd/mm/2026] Summary The post shows how to resize images on demand. Originals are stored in S3; when a user requests a size that does not exist yet, an S3 redirect rule sends the request to API Gateway, Lambda downloads the original, resizes it, saves it to S3 and redirects the user to the new file. Later requests are served straight from S3.
Relevance to SnapThumb This post helps compare two designs. The original creates images when someone views them (lazy), which suits many different sizes. SnapThumb creates them on upload (eager) through S3 events, which suits one fixed size that should be ready immediately. This comparison feeds the risk and future-work parts of the report.
Translation [The Vietnamese translation lives on the Vietnamese version of this page]

title: Create the Function and S3 Trigger
content:
Step 1: Create the function AWS Lambda → Create function → Author from scratch. Name: snapthumb-thumbnail, Runtime: Python 3.12, Architecture: x86_64 → Create function. Replace lambda_function.py with the code below → Deploy. """SnapThumb - hàm Lambda tạo ảnh thu nhỏ. Kích hoạt bởi sự kiện S3 ObjectCreated trên tiền tố uploads/. Đọc ảnh gốc, tạo thumbnail JPEG (cạnh dài tối đa THUMB_MAX_SIZE px), ghi vào thumbnails/, rồi cập nhật trạng thái và thông số vào DynamoDB. """ import io import logging import os import urllib.parse from datetime import datetime, timezone import boto3 from PIL import Image, ImageOps logger = logging.getLogger() logger.setLevel(logging.INFO) UPLOAD_PREFIX = "uploads/" THUMB_PREFIX = "thumbnails/" THUMB_MAX_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("THUMB_MAX_SIZE", "320")) JPEG_QUALITY = 85 _s3 = None _table = None def s3(): global _s3 if _s3 is None: _s3 = boto3.client("s3") return _s3 def table(): global _table if _table is None: _table = boto3.resource("dynamodb").Table(os.environ["TABLE_NAME"]) return _table def make_thumbnail(data, max_size=THUMB_MAX_SIZE): """Trả về (bytes JPEG của thumbnail, (rộng, cao) gốc, (rộng, cao) thumbnail).""" with Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as original: img = ImageOps.exif_transpose(original) # xoay đúng chiều theo EXIF của ảnh điện thoại original_size = img.size if img.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") or (img.mode == "P" and "transparency" in img.info): # JPEG không có kênh trong suốt: đặt ảnh lên nền trắng rgba = img.convert("RGBA") img = Image.new("RGB", rgba.size, (255, 255, 255)) img.paste(rgba, mask=rgba.split()[-1]) elif img.mode not in ("RGB", "L"): img = img.convert("RGB") img.thumbnail((max_size, max_size), Image.LANCZOS) # giữ nguyên tỉ lệ out = io.BytesIO() img.save(out, "JPEG", quality=JPEG_QUALITY, optimize=True, progressive=True) return out.getvalue(), original_size, img.size def image_id_from_key(key): name = key[len(UPLOAD_PREFIX):] return name.rsplit(".", 1)[0] def parse_time(value): return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")) def process_record(record): bucket = record["s3"]["bucket"]["name"] key = urllib.parse.unquote_plus(record["s3"]["object"]["key"]) if not key.startswith(UPLOAD_PREFIX): logger.info("Skip %s (not under %s)", key, UPLOAD_PREFIX) return image_id = image_id_from_key(key) thumb_key = f"{THUMB_PREFIX}{image_id}.jpg" try: data = s3().get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)["Body"].read() thumb, (ow, oh), (tw, th) = make_thumbnail(data) s3().put_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=thumb_key, Body=thumb, ContentType="image/jpeg") now = datetime.now(timezone.utc) processing_ms = int((now - parse_time(record["eventTime"])).total_seconds() * 1000) table().update_item( Key={"id": image_id}, UpdateExpression=( "SET #s = :s, thumbKey = :tk, originalBytes = :ob, thumbBytes = :tb, " "originalWidth = :ow, originalHeight = :oh, thumbWidth = :tw, thumbHeight = :th, " "processedAt = :pa, processingMs = :pm REMOVE errorMessage" ), ExpressionAttributeNames={"#s": "status"}, ExpressionAttributeValues={ ":s": "DONE", ":tk": thumb_key, ":ob": len(data), ":tb": len(thumb), ":ow": ow, ":oh": oh, ":tw": tw, ":th": th, ":pa": now.isoformat(), ":pm": max(processing_ms, 0), }, ) logger.info("Thumbnail %s: %dx%d -> %dx%d, %d -> %d bytes", image_id, ow, oh, tw, th, len(data), len(thumb)) except Exception as err: # ảnh hỏng hoặc không đọc được: đánh dấu lỗi để giao diện hiển thị logger.exception("Failed to process %s", key) table().update_item( Key={"id": image_id}, UpdateExpression="SET #s = :s, errorMessage = :e", ExpressionAttributeNames={"#s": "status"}, ExpressionAttributeValues={":s": "FAILED", ":e": str(err)[:300]}, ) def handler(event, context): for record in event.get("Records", []): process_record(record) return {"processed": len(event.get("Records", []))} lambda_handler = handler # tên hàm mặc định của Lambda console / default handler name in the console What the code does Part Explanation make_thumbnail Opens the image, fixes EXIF rotation, flattens transparency onto white, shrinks so the longest edge is at most 320 px keeping the aspect ratio, saves as JPEG quality 85 image_id_from_key uploads/3f9c.jpg → 3f9c, the item’s key in DynamoDB key.startswith(UPLOAD_PREFIX) Safety check: ignores anything outside uploads/ processing_ms Time from the S3 event to the finished thumbnail except branch A broken file is marked FAILED with the error, so the page can show it Step 2: Configuration Configuration → General configuration → Edit: Memory 1024 MB (more memory also means more CPU, so resizing is faster), Timeout 30 sec. Configuration → Environment variables → Edit: TABLE_NAME = snapthumb-images, THUMB_MAX_SIZE = 320. Code tab, bottom → Layers → Add a layer → Custom layers → pillow-py312, version 1 → Add. Step 3: Permissions Configuration → Permissions → click the role name → Add permissions → Create inline policy → JSON. Replace YOURNAME and ACCOUNT_ID, then name it snapthumb-thumbnail-access.
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "ReadOriginals", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::snapthumb-images-YOURNAME/uploads/*" }, { "Sid": "WriteThumbnails", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::snapthumb-images-YOURNAME/thumbnails/*" }, { "Sid": "UpdateMetadata", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "dynamodb:UpdateItem", "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:ACCOUNT_ID:table/snapthumb-images" } ] } Step 4: Add the S3 trigger In the function overview, Add trigger → S3. Bucket: snapthumb-images-<your-name>, Event types: All object create events, Prefix: uploads/. Tick the acknowledgement about recursive invocation → Add. 📷 Insert screenshot: function overview with the S3 trigger and Pillow layer → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/02-trigger.png
Never leave the prefix empty. The function writes to the same bucket; without uploads/ it would trigger itself for every thumbnail.
Step 5: Test Upload a photo to the bucket’s uploads/ folder in the S3 console. After a few seconds, open thumbnails/: a .jpg with the same name should be there. In DynamoDB → Explore items, the new item has status = DONE. 📷 Insert screenshot: thumbnail in thumbnails/ and the DONE item → static/images/5-Workshop/5.5/03-test.png

title: Proposal
content:
SnapThumb An automatic image thumbnail service on AWS 1. Executive Summary SnapThumb is a web app where users upload images and get thumbnails back within seconds. It follows an event-driven architecture: as soon as an image lands in Amazon S3, S3 emits an event and AWS Lambda runs automatically to create the thumbnail, with no server running all the time. The whole system is serverless, and the demo costs close to 0 USD per month.
2. Problem Statement Current Problem Phone photos are often 3–8 MB and 4000 px or more wide. Showing originals in lists, galleries or product pages makes pages slow and wastes bandwidth, especially on mobile networks. Resizing on an always-on server means paying for it when nobody uploads, and handling bursts yourself. Solution Users upload images directly from the browser to Amazon S3 with a time-limited link (presigned POST). S3 triggers AWS Lambda for each new image; Lambda uses Pillow to create a 320 px thumbnail and stores it back in S3. Image details (status, dimensions, size, processing time) are written to Amazon DynamoDB for the UI. Benefits Thumbnails are about 90–98% smaller than originals, so pages load faster. Pay only when images are processed; idle cost is close to zero. Scales automatically: 1 or 100 images at once, Lambda runs them in parallel. New processing steps (compression, watermarking, detection) can be added without touching the upload path. 3. Solution Architecture Solution Architecture Main flow (1–9):
The user loads the static web page from Amazon S3. The page sends POST /uploads (file name, type, size) to Amazon API Gateway. API Gateway invokes the API Lambda. The API Lambda validates the file, writes a PENDING record to DynamoDB and returns an upload link valid for 5 minutes. The browser uploads the image directly to S3, under uploads/. S3 emits an ObjectCreated event and invokes the Thumbnail Lambda. The Thumbnail Lambda reads the original, creates the thumbnail and stores it under thumbnails/. The Thumbnail Lambda updates the DynamoDB record to DONE with dimensions, sizes and processing time. The page calls GET /images every 1.5 seconds; once the image is done, the API Lambda returns view links valid for 1 hour and the thumbnail appears. Monitoring and security: both Lambda functions log to Amazon CloudWatch. Each function has its own IAM role with only the permissions it needs. The image bucket is not public.
AWS Services Used Service Layer Role Amazon S3 (web bucket) Frontend Hosts the static web UI Amazon API Gateway API HTTPS endpoints POST /uploads, GET /images, DELETE /images/{id}; CORS; throttling AWS Lambda (API) Backend Validates files, signs time-limited upload/view links, lists and deletes images Amazon S3 (image bucket) Backend Stores originals (uploads/) and thumbnails (thumbnails/); emits events on new images AWS Lambda (Thumbnail) Backend Creates thumbnails with Pillow Amazon DynamoDB Backend Stores each image’s status and details Amazon CloudWatch Monitoring Logs and metrics for both Lambda functions AWS IAM Security Least-privilege permissions per function AWS CloudFormation Deployment Creates and deletes all infrastructure from code Component Design Frontend A single plain index.html (HTML, CSS, JavaScript): drag-and-drop for multiple images, gallery, per-image status. Checks file type (JPEG, PNG, WebP) and size (up to 10 MB) before upload. Backend API Lambda (Python 3.12): three routes; issues presigned POSTs with conditions on file type and size, so S3 itself rejects invalid files. Thumbnail Lambda (Python 3.12 + Pillow): keeps the aspect ratio, honours EXIF rotation, flattens transparent PNGs onto white, never enlarges small images, outputs JPEG at quality 85. Originals and thumbnails live under different prefixes; the trigger listens only to uploads/, so there is no infinite loop. Data DynamoDB, partition key id, on-demand capacity. Each image stores file name, status (PENDING, DONE, FAILED), dimensions and sizes before/after, and processing time. Security The image bucket blocks all public access; images are viewable only through time-limited links. Upload links expire after 5 minutes and are limited to 10 MB and allowed types. API Gateway is throttled to 10 requests per second. 4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases Prepare the account, region and cost alerts. Create the image bucket, DynamoDB table and Pillow layer. Create the Thumbnail Lambda and S3 trigger. Create the API Lambda and API Gateway. Write and host the web UI. Automate with CloudFormation; test, monitor, clean up. Technical Requirements Programming Languages Python 3.12 (Lambda) HTML, CSS, JavaScript (UI) Libraries boto3 (included in Lambda), Pillow 11 (image processing), moto (mocked AWS for tests) Tools AWS Management Console, AWS CloudShell, AWS CLI, Visual Studio Code, Git, Hugo 5. Timeline & Milestones Week Work 1–5 AWS fundamentals: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway 6 Event-driven architecture, choosing the project, writing the proposal 7 Image bucket, DynamoDB, Pillow packaging 8 Thumbnail Lambda and S3 trigger 9 API Lambda, API Gateway and web UI 10 Automation with CloudFormation; testing 11 Write the workshop; publish the report on GitHub Pages 12 Demo, cleanup, wrap-up 6. Budget Estimation Infrastructure Cost Estimate Assumptions: ap-southeast-1; 1,000 images/month of about 3 MB each; each image viewed about 20 times.
Item Estimated cost (USD/month) Amazon S3 (about 3 GB originals + thumbnails, requests) ~0.08 AWS Lambda (1,000 thumbnails × ~1 s × 1 GB, plus API calls) ~0.00 (Free Tier) Amazon DynamoDB on-demand (tens of thousands of reads/writes) ~0.01 Amazon API Gateway HTTP API (about 25,000 requests) ~0.03 Amazon CloudWatch Logs ~0.00 (Free Tier) Total < 0.20 These are estimates based on list prices, which can change. [Insert your AWS Pricing Calculator link here]
Cost Control Guidelines Create a 5 USD AWS Budget from day one. Delete all resources after the demo with destroy.sh (section 5.10). 7. Risk Assessment Risk Matrix Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation Infinite loop: Lambda writes to the bucket and triggers itself Medium High Trigger listens only to uploads/; thumbnails go to thumbnails/ Malicious or oversized uploads Medium Medium Presigned POST limits type and size to 10 MB; Lambda marks unreadable files FAILED User images exposed Low High Private bucket; view links expire after 1 hour Unexpected charges Low Medium AWS Budgets, API throttling, cleanup after the demo Missing service quota on a new account Low High Use only core services; check quotas before choosing an architecture 8. Expected Outcomes Technical Outcomes A working web app: upload multiple images, get thumbnails in 1–3 seconds, view and delete them. Thumbnails at least 90% smaller than phone photos. All infrastructure rebuilt with one command; automated tests included. Practical Value Applies to any image-heavy system: galleries, online shops, profile photos in a student management system. A foundation for further image-processing steps using the same event-driven pattern.

title: Automate with CloudFormation
content:
Everything in 5.3–5.7 can be created by one template. This is Infrastructure as Code: the system is described in a file, so it can be rebuilt identically, reviewed and versioned.
What the template contains infra/template.yaml in the source package creates: the image bucket (CORS, S3 trigger), the DynamoDB table, both Lambda functions with their IAM roles and log groups, the HTTP API with three routes and throttling, and the website bucket.
A circular dependency to solve The bucket’s trigger needs the function, the function’s permission needs the bucket’s ARN, and the function’s IAM policy also needs the bucket. Referencing the bucket resource from both would create a cycle CloudFormation refuses. The template breaks it by building the bucket name from the stack name: ${AWS::StackName}-images-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}. The permission and the policy use that string, not a reference to the bucket.
Deploy with one command In CloudShell, upload snapthumb.zip, then:
unzip -oq snapthumb.zip && cd snapthumb && bash deploy.sh deploy.sh runs four steps: create or update the stack; package the Thumbnail function with Pillow; upload both functions’ code; upload the web page with config.js filled in. It prints the website address at the end.
📷 Insert screenshot: CloudFormation stack Resources tab → static/images/5-Workshop/5.9/01-stack.png
Automated tests backend/test_app.py runs the whole flow against mocked AWS (moto): create an upload link, upload, run the thumbnail handler, list, delete, plus broken files, transparent PNGs, portrait and small images, and invalid input.
